title: Chapter 157: Victims
html:
A stench hung in the air, growing stronger as Chen Ge approached the Third Sick Hall. The connecting passage was locked, with a steel door separating the two buildings.

Through a narrow gap, he could make out the corridor beyond. Tables and chairs lay overturned among a jumble of mattresses, their swollen shapes suggesting something hidden underneath.

Beside the rusted steel door, Chen Ge fixed his gaze on the keyhole.

“A double-sided lock?” Most mental hospitals used double-sided locks. In an emergency, the door could be locked from either side to prevent entry to seal up an entire area.

The minor detail caught his attention. He took out the key Wang Haiming had left behind and tested it. Years without maintenance had rusted the lock almost solid, and the key barely entered.

“It would have been too fortunate if this fit.” After comparing the key’s length and teeth with the keyhole, he pocketed it. Most doors elsewhere in the hospital used single-sided locks with openings far too small for Wang Haiming’s key.

Wang Haiming carried this key out of the Third Sick Hall, so its lock should be somewhere inside that building. The hall had ten rooms but only nine recorded patients. Could Wang Haiming have been the missing occupant of Room 3?

He had no way to confirm the theory. Doctor Gao had searched every available record and found nothing connected to Room 3. Wang Haiming alone couldn’t have justified erasing every trace.

The hospital’s mysteries ran deep. Chen Ge cared little about everything that had happened five years ago; he wanted only his parents’ clue and a method for closing the “door.”

Flashlight in hand, he entered the third-floor corridor and passed each room cautiously. “Is the person I saw hiding behind one of these doors?”

At the far end, he stopped before a room whose purpose was unclear. A heavy mildew odor seeped through its unusual door, from which hung a brand-new padlock.

“No rust. Like the lock on the first hall’s entrance, this one is new.” Wang Haiming’s key failed again. After checking the dark corridor behind him and confirming that he was alone, Chen Ge raised the mallet and struck the door.

“Good thing it’s wood. I’d never break through steel.” The door gave way, releasing a suffocating wave of mildew. Patients’ clothes and discarded mattresses filled the room in a low hill.

“This must have been the second hall’s laundry room.” His chest camera captured everything, including his narration. The danger prevented him from relaxing enough to chat with the audience, so he simply voiced every sight and thought, turning the broadcast into a live supernatural documentary.

Mildew overpowered even the hall’s stench and left his skin feeling clammy. Suppressing his revulsion, he stepped inside.

Several washing machines and specialized sanitizing units lined the walls of the large room. Dirty clothes and old mattresses occupied everything else.

“The room itself looks ordinary. Why lock it?” He focused on the mound of laundry. Holding his breath, he used the mallet to peel away layer after layer. “Something is hidden beneath this.”

He worked faster. As he dragged aside another stained garment, the mallet struck something hard with a metallic clang.

“An iron cage?” He shoved away a mattress, and the sight beneath it stopped his heart: a young woman with a shaved head was imprisoned inside.

A dirty pillowcase gagged her, and her hands were bound to the bars. Wild-eyed and frantic, she shook her head at Chen Ge, waved her tied hands, and kicked against the cage.

Stunned, Chen Ge stared. He had never expected to uncover a living person beneath the laundry. The chat erupted so violently that the flood of comments made the broadcast lag.

He stepped back but remained composed. First, he shut the door and dragged a washing machine across it to prevent an attack from behind. Only after securing the entrance did he approach the cage.

“Can you understand me?” The woman thrashed harder when he came near, making communication impossible. “She has no visible wounds and no grease around her mouth. This isn’t the person dragged from the first hall. There must be others here.”

Rummaging through the remaining laundry, he discovered that the terrible stench concealed three iron cages. Their arrangement formed the character 品, mirroring the hospital’s three buildings.

The woman occupied the center. To her left crouched an emaciated man of about seventy, grease staining his lips and fingers. To her right sat a pallid middle-aged man who looked as though he had not seen sunlight in years. Only that man met Chen Ge’s eyes, his expression mingling excitement, disgust, and fear.

“Three victims?”

The discovery overturned every expectation. A troubling possibility occurred to him, and he tightened his grip on the mallet before retreating to a safe distance.

When encountering strangers in a dangerous place, the safest course was to trust nothing they said and keep out of reach. The true captor might be hiding among the apparent victims.

He circled the cages. They were unmistakably built for animals; a human occupant could not even turn around inside one.

“Three cages, yet only the woman is gagged and bound.” More questions arose. If all three were victims, why restrain only the physically weakest one?

The old man’s face remained vacant, while expressions flickered across the middle-aged man’s. Neither had bound limbs, yet neither called for help. They simply sat in silence and watched Chen Ge.

While the livestream audience erupted, Chen Ge remained calm. Standing before the cages, he asked, “How long have you been held here?”
